For NER, predictions from all batches are merged via set union; for RE, each instance is routed to the batch containing its gold type (oracle routing). We test four NER modes: (i)~\textbf{single\_pass}, the undecomposed baseline; (ii)~\textbf{sdgd\_zero}, SCS-guided partitioning; (iii)~\textbf{random\_batch}, random partitioning with matched batch sizes; and (iv)~\textbf{per\_type}, each type extracted in isolation. Every mode falls below the single-pass NER baseline: SDGD obtains F1\,=\,0.251, random batching 0.320, per-type 0.292, versus 0.445 for single-pass (Table~\ref{tab:sdgd_results}, Appendix~\ref{sec:appendix_sdgd}).
\paragraph{Merge amplification in NER.}

-The core failure mechanism is \emph{merge amplification}: presenting the same text to the model $k$ times with different type subsets causes each pass to independently generate entity predictions, and union merge accumulates all of them into a single output. Union merge retains all predictions, so false positives scale with $k$ while true positives are bounded by the fixed set of gold entities.
